results.query: Civiqs Donald Trump approval rating latest

results.content:
Nationally, 35 percent of voters approve of Trump's job performance while 59 percent disapprove as of August 19, leaving him significantly underwater with a net approval rating of -24, according to Civiqs' rolling online tracking poll of registered voters. The survey has garnered 124,759 responses since January 20, 2025, when Trump was inaugurated for a second term. [...] According to the Civiqs poll, Trump has the highest net approval rating in Wyoming, where 56 percent of voters approve of his performance and 35 disapprove—giving him a net approval rating of +22 when rounding up.

His net approval rating is also positive in several other states that make up the Republican heartland:

results.content:
Trump remains weakest among younger voters. Among those aged 18 to 34, just 22 percent approve of his job performance, compared with 72 percent who disapprove, according to the newest Civiqs data.

Among voters aged 35 to 49, approval stands at 29 percent, while 63 percent disapprove.

Independents also remain negative, with 28 percent approving and 64 percent disapproving. Women disapprove by a 65-to-30 margin, while men are divided at 53 percent disapprove to 42 percent approve. [...] At a comparable point before those elections, Civiqs polling showed Trump on 43 percent approval and 53 percent disapproval, for a net approval rating of -10. results.content:
When asked in April 2025, Trump's first three months were rated at 61% approval by Oklahoman polltakers. Now in August 2026, Trump remains at 52% approval in Oklahoma.

Nationally, Trump has an unfavorable majority across all ages, education levels, genders, and races. Trump's only favorability among Civiqs' demographics is found in the 82% of Republicans who remain faithful to the president. results.content: Civiqs, which offers regular updates from its online surveys, pegged approval in Colorado of Trump’s job performance at 31%, with disapproval at 64% on July 30 (4% said they neither approved nor disapproved). [...] Drew Linzer, the director of Civiqs, previously told the USA TODAY Network the firm uses advanced and proprietary modeling to develop results from online surveys of around 200 to 250 registered voters daily across the country. Voters in Colorado and other states are represented in the sample "proportional to the sizes of those states in the US population." Those results are part of the process used in calculating Trump’s approval rating in each state.

results.content:
President Donald Trump’s job approval rating in Alabama remains above water, though it has declined from the high point he reached at the start of his second term, according to the latest tracking data from Civiqs.

The survey shows 53% of Alabama voters approve of Trump’s job performance, while 40% disapprove. Another 8% said they neither approve nor disapprove.
